target: degenerate -- Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player

findings.defect: The clause "for m = 2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game" is verified only at m<=2. The exhibited m=3 and m=4 witnesses are harmonic normal forms with NON-DYADIC entries and were never built as fair-coin SSGs; they are therefore not instances in the sense of def:ssg, and their realisability is exactly the unverified (v4) dictionary question.
findings.evidence: deg_m3_run4.json carries q = 26566357/27305639040 and deg_m4_run6.json carries q = 362854819/4510476448. I factored the denominators: 27305639040 = 2^7*3*5*29*653*751 and 4510476448 = 2^5*17*47*67*2633. t_deg3.py/t_deg6.py construct them by `newQ = QB[v][a] - gap` where gap is a value difference of a game whose values have odd denominators (the same phenomenon as the 43111 in degen:prop-nolin), and they check everything through the normal-form class OP only -- build_ssg is never called on them (it would not terminate: dyadic_depth loops on a non-dyadic denominator). Every other instance in the route IS built and checked from the game; these two are not. The tie is a codimension-one condition, so rounding q to a dyadic destroys it, and the route's own random sweeps at m=4 never produced a degenerate game with a run longer than 3. The LaTeX nevertheless says "explicit instances ... are recorded in deg_m3_run4.json", which in this paper's usage means an SSG.

findings.defect: Presented in the summary as "No amount of chaining raises the run length above m + O(1)", but the hypothesis "no vertex of B_1,...,B_{r-1} switches after the round at which B_r wakes" is precisely the mechanism every known exponential policy-iteration lower bound uses (a competing action is offered and withdrawn later, so lower blocks switch again). The corollary therefore rules out only one-shot chaining, covers none of M1-M6 or def:bsi, and duplicates in spirit an argument the paper already makes.
findings.evidence: rem:closed-now-or-never (frontier.tex lines 3304-3330) already states: "The published exponential lower bounds ... delay a switch into an already attractive cycle by offering the vertex a competing action of larger appeal and withdrawing it later. With out-degree two there is no third action ... A Max vertex whose successor is another Max vertex simulates a three-way choice one round later, and def:damping makes such a tree cheap, so the postponement can be reintroduced with a lag ... The proposition covers none of M1-M6 or def:bsi: it is a law of runs, not a barrier against algorithms." degen:cor-gate is the quantitative version of the same observation under a hypothesis that forbids exactly the lag. It does not cite rem:closed-now-or-never.

findings.defect: Its lower-bound content, h*_1(m) >= m for one-player stopping games, is already in the paper, and the construction is the textbook chain MDP on which one improving switch fires per round. Neither is attributed.
findings.evidence: def:ladder's L_n has Vmin empty, is stopping, has |Vmax| = n, and rem:ladder (frontier.tex line 4672) records "The all-switches rule terminates on L_n in exactly n iterations (exact computation, n = 1,...,12)", so h*_1(n) >= n is already established. rem:ladder also attributes the family shape to Melekopoglou-Condon, whose two-action instances are chains of exactly this kind. degen:prop-staircase's genuinely new content is only the zero-tie structure (in L_n every v_i is switchable at round 0, so L_n is NOT a timer), which is what makes degen:thm-timer sharp; the lower bound itself is a rediscovery.

findings.defect: The perturbed object is asserted to be "a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG" for small RATIONAL eps, delta, but a normal form with arbitrary rational entries need not be realisable by fair coins; prop:oneplayer-lp, which is then invoked, is stated for SSGs. Repairable in one word (dyadic eps, delta and dyadic pi', rho' keep the rows dyadic and hence buildable), but as written the lemma steps outside def:ssg.
findings.evidence: degen.tex, statement of degen:lem-gperturb: "for a generic admissible (pi',rho') and all sufficiently small rationals delta>0 and epsilon>0 the game with rows (p+eps(pi+delta pi'), q+eps(rho+delta rho')) is a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG". The route's own builder build.py realises only dyadic normal forms. The lemma is not load-bearing for degen:thm-no-seven (which uses only degen:cor-onetie), so this is confined to the sufficient condition (**). I checked the mathematics of the lemma itself: the derivative formula Delta(sigma,v) = rho_{v,abar}-rho_{v,a} + (pi^{v,abar}-pi^{v,a}).val_sigma + (p^{v,abar}-p^{v,a}).u_sigma matched exact numerical derivatives of the incidence gap on 40 random one-player normal forms, 0 mismatches.

findings.defect: "no stopping SSG ... has an all-switches run whose resolution lies in the orbit of s12" uses "the resolution" as if it were well defined, but thm:flat-resolution's corner choice is arbitrary on flat classes off the run, so a game has many resolutions. The statement should quantify ("some resolution with c_{A(sigma_t)} = sigma_t"). Combined with degen:rem-five's admission that other height-12 classes of the 5-cube exist and cannot be enumerated, the proposition asserts almost nothing.
findings.evidence: cor:ceiling-general fixes corners only on the run ("extend it arbitrarily to the remaining classes"). At m=4 the ambiguity is harmless because h*(4)=7 is attained by a single orbit, so every admissible resolution lands in it; at m=5 it is not harmless. I reproduced the computation itself exactly (s12 is a USO, acyclic, BA height 12, not Holt-Klee; the (F1)-blocks of dimension >= 1 are the seven edges {12,14},{1,3},{13,15},{29,31},{18,22},{0,16},{14,30}; 96 candidate partitions; the unique nontrivial survivor is {0,16} at start 0).

findings.defect: Item (a) is not a new result: it is prop:oneplayer-lp's own printed proof, in which nondegeneracy is used only in the final paragraph. Items (b) and (c) are one line each from lem:switch and lem:trichotomy. Numbering this as a proposition inflates the count; it is a remark on an existing proof.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex lines 4029-4052: the paragraph establishing "the vertices of X(G) are exactly the 2^m points y^sigma ... X(G) is a simple m-polytope whose graph is the m-cube and whose faces are its subcubes; obj(y^sigma) = sum val_sigma" never mentions nondegeneracy, which enters only at "which is nonzero by nondegeneracy" in the last paragraph. The route's own proof of degen:prop-partial-lp says "(a) is the proof of prop:oneplayer-lp verbatim", so the rediscovery is labelled, not hidden.

findings.defect: Almost certainly folklore in the MDP literature (the positive-value set of a max-reachability MDP is an attractor, and under policy improvement it grows by one backward layer per round, so it stabilises within |states| rounds). The route gives no attribution. From memory, unchecked against any source.
findings.evidence: The theorem's proof is exactly a backward attractor chain: w alive at sigma_s and dead at sigma_{s-1} forces a witness Max vertex whose other action's target was alive at sigma_{s-1} and dead at sigma_{s-2}. The paper computes the same object non-iteratively at lem:det-game and thm:avg-acyclic ("attractor" arguments, frontier.tex lines 1826-1847). I checked the proof line by line and it is correct, including the s=1 boundary case; the statement is new to frontier.tex (grep for dead/wake/attractor turns up only def:attractor and the unrelated def:dead of the random-facet section).

findings.defect: The sweep supporting condition (**) does not touch the regime where (**) could matter: the randomly generated degenerate games have all-switches runs of length at most 3 (m=4), 4 (m=5) and 4 (m=6), against ceilings h*_1(4) = 6 and h*(5) = 12. So the report is not merely 'random sampling is not evidence' -- the sampled runs are structurally incapable of being counterexamples to L <= h*_HK. The route says 'this is a report, not evidence', which is honest, but does not say the regime is empty.
findings.evidence: sweep_m4.log: "games=300 degenerate=165 runs=2640 longest run=4"; sweep_m5.log: "longest run=5"; sweep_m6.log: "longest run=4"; sweep2_m4.log: "games=200 degenerate=112 runs=1792 longest=3"; sweep2_m5.log: "longest=4". The single (*)-failure found (degen:prop-nolin) sits on a run of length 2.

verdict:
SUMMARY. The central theorem is real, correct and independently reproducible; I re-derived every load-bearing computation from scratch and found no error in it. The route is, however, mostly a hypothesis-cleanup on one constant-size instance, plus a clean negative result about its own mechanism. Nineteen labels carry about six results' worth of content. Integrating the whole file would make the paper worse; integrating a trimmed half of it makes it better.

1. IS IT NEW? Yes for the core, with two unattributed rediscoveries.
NEW AND NOT IN frontier.tex: degen:lem-seven-flat, degen:thm-no-seven, degen:cor-hstar-one (the m=4 value h*_1(4)=6), degen:cor-onetie, degen:lem-perturb, degen:prop-nolin, degen:prop-res-nonhk, degen:thm-timer, degen:cor-gate, degen:prop-family. degen:thm-no-seven genuinely repairs cor:seven-two-player, whose nondegeneracy hypothesis rem:oneplayer-lp explicitly flags as load-bearing and open ("the corollary ... says nothing about degenerate ones"). That is a flagged hole in the standing paper, and the route closes it at m=4.
ALREADY THERE UNDER ANOTHER NAME: degen:prop-partial-lp(a) is prop:oneplayer-lp's own printed proof (nondegeneracy enters only in its last paragraph); the route says so. degen:prop-staircase's lower bound h*_1(m) >= m is already in the paper via def:ladder + rem:ladder (L_n is one-player, stopping, |Vmax| = n, all-switches run exactly n) and the construction is the textbook two-action chain MDP; neither is cited.
STANDARD MATHEMATICS UNACKNOWLEDGED: (i) the tie-breaking device of degen:lem-perturb is textbook lexicographic/symbolic perturbation of a degenerate LP objective (Charnes; Dantzig-Orden-Wolfe -- from memory, unchecked); the route attributes Holt-Klee and Gaertner-Morris-Ruest but not the perturbation technique. Its real content -- that the standard perturbation need NOT preserve the all-switches run, degen:prop-nolin -- is new and is the good part. (ii) degen:thm-timer is very likely folklore (attractor growth under policy improvement on max-reachability MDPs); unattributed.

2. CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No oracle, no target-equivalent assumption, no claimed algorithm, no claimed polynomial class, so items 2a and 2c do not arise. The one barrier-flavoured item, degen:cor-gate, covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi -- it is a law about run shapes, not about algorithms -- and its hypothesis "no vertex of B_1..B_{r-1} switches after B_r wakes" excludes exactly the offer-then-withdraw mechanism that rem:closed-now-or-never already identifies as how every published exponential lower bound works. So its headline "no amount of chaining raises the run length above m + O(1)" is an overstatement of a hypothesis-heavy corollary; the paper already contains the qualitative version. degen:prop-family IS a legitimate family (I rebuilt it: fair coins, out-degree two, stopping by the trap test, run recomputed from the explicit game at s = 0,4,8 with a cross-checked solver, L = m+2 and ties 4s+C(s,2) exactly as claimed) -- but a family of run length m+2 is worth one sentence, not a proposition with a five-column table, since rem:ladder already gives length m.

3. IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Yes, and unusually so, with one exception. I reproduced independently: (a) an exhaustive C enumeration of the 4-cube -- 5541744 USOs, 4792176 acyclic, heights 16/264608/1800000/2072832/599424/54912/384, so exactly 384 AUSOs of height 7, and they are precisely the orbit of the route's representative; my own vertex-capacity max-flow test says none is Holt-Klee, and an explicit height-6 AUSO is, so h*_HK(4) = 6 and the pillar of degen:thm-no-seven stands without relying on the solo round's census file; (b) my own from-scratch (F1)-(F4) enumeration: 768 (outmap,start) pairs, exactly 384 admit a partition with a block of dimension >= 1, in each case unique and the single edge containing the start, and each height-7 outmap has exactly four (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1, all pairwise disjoint edges -- degen:lem-seven-flat confirmed; (c) the same for the 5-cube s12 -- confirmed; (d) degen:prop-nolin from the printed rows: S = (9,10,9,8,9,12,9,12,5,4,7,6,1,0,1,0), D = (6,0,6,0,6,2,6,2,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2), run 7->11->13, two flat incidences at x_2 with opposite actions, y^15-y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7-y^5), and as an explicit fair-coin SSG N = 34 with 28 average vertices, stopping, same run; (e) the Delta formula of degen:lem-gperturb against exact numerical derivatives, 40 instances, 0 mismatches. The exception is degen:cor-hstar-one's degenerate-attainment clause (finding 1): those two "explicit instances" are non-dyadic normal forms that were never built as games. Separately, the sweeps supporting (**) are not merely random -- their runs are at most 3-5 long against ceilings 6 and 12, so they never enter the regime where (**) could fail; the route calls the sweeps "a report, not evidence" but does not say the regime is empty.

4. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's gap ("every one-player stopping SSG has L <= h*_HK(m)") is stated at the right place but is softer than the truth in two ways. Sharper: for every one-player stopping SSG and every all-switches run, some admissible perturbation direction must make EVERY flat incidence on the run strictly non-switchable; this is proved ONLY in the two cases where the extremal orientation combinatorially forces at most one flat incidence, on a single edge at the start (m=4 height 7; one named m=5 height-12 class), and degen:prop-nolin exhibits a run where the objective-only version of that condition provably fails, so the general statement needs a non-linear completion of the partial orientation. And the deeper point the route does not make: even the general statement would buy the project nothing on its own, because h*_HK(m) is not known to be polynomial OR superpolynomial -- so the route's own reformulation of the pivot's one-player half ("is Howard's rule superpolynomial with two actions" becomes "is h*_HK superpolynomial") rests on the equality h*_1 = h*_HK, for which there is exactly ONE nontrivial data point (m = 4; at m <= 3 the two coincide with h* for free). Presenting 1,2,4,6 as a pattern is one measurement dressed as four.

5. INTEGRATE? YES, TRIMMED -- roughly halved. Integrating all nineteen labels makes the paper worse by volume: it adds a proposition that is an existing proof, a family with linear growth, a table of five sizes for a constant-plus-linear law, a duplicate of thm:ladder's all-switches count, and a hypothesis-heavy corollary that restates rem:closed-now-or-never. WORTH INTEGRATING, as a subsection after prop:oneplayer-lp: degen:lem-perturb, degen:cor-onetie, degen:lem-seven-flat, degen:thm-no-seven, degen:cor-hstar-one (with the degenerate-attainment clause deleted or weakened to m<=2 until a dyadic witness exists), degen:prop-nolin (the most reusable single item here: an exact, explicit, engineered obstruction with a Gordan certificate, and the shape a future route should try to iterate), and degen:thm-timer with degen:prop-staircase compressed into one proposition that cites rem:ladder for the run length and claims only the zero-tie structure. NOT WORTH SEPARATE RESULTS: degen:prop-partial-lp (fold into rem:oneplayer-lp as "nondegeneracy enters only at the edges"), degen:lem-gperturb (a remark recording the sufficient condition (**) and its dyadic caveat), degen:prop-five and degen:rem-five (one remark), degen:prop-res-nonhk (one sentence appended to rem:oneplayer-lp, which currently asserts the fact without an instance), degen:cor-gate and degen:prop-family (one remark, explicitly cross-referenced to rem:closed-now-or-never and explicitly saying it covers none of M1-M6 or def:bsi). Two dangling references, deg:prop-zeroties and deg:prop-hk5, must be restated or dropped; the route flags them. Net effect of the trimmed version: the paper gains an unconditional cor:seven-two-player, a new constant h*_1(4) = 6, a sharp linear cap on zero-tie sequencing, and one genuinely engineered counterexample -- while the honest headline is that this is bookkeeping of the same register as rem:flat, and it moves nothing on the pivot.
